After 1945 Germany was carved into zones. This map shows a plan to divide Japan the same way, and why it never happened.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ Per the map: the Soviet Union takes Hokkaido and northern Honshu, the US central Honshu, the UK western Honshu and Kyushu, and China Shikoku. Tokyo is jointly run, much like Berlin.

2/ The Allies did originally plan to divide Japan for occupation, as with Germany. The final plan went another way: General Douglas MacArthur became Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers with direct control of the four main islands.
3/ The Soviet Union never occupied any part of the home islands, largely because of US opposition. Stalin declined to place Soviet troops under MacArthur's command.
4/ The Soviets took South Sakhalin, the Kuril Islands and northern Korea instead. An Allied council and a Far Eastern Commission supervised Japan, but the US ran the occupation.
5/ It lasted from the surrender on 2 September 1945 until the San Francisco Treaty took effect on 28 April 1952.
6/ Okinawa stayed under US administration after that. Iwo Jima returned to Japan in 1968 and most of Okinawa in 1972.
Would a divided Japan have become another Korea? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
